comment: Exported symbols with zero non-test reference in this module and in an external checkout, when one is checked via check_symbol_wiring.py's external-checkout flag or SDK_CONSUMER_PATH, declared on purpose. This repo is a public SDK and names no specific caller here. check_symbol_wiring.py fails on any such symbol missing here, or on a stale entry: one whose symbol no longer appears in any api/*.txt lock, or one that has gained a real caller since the entry was written. permanent=false means an internal or external caller is expected later, named in target. The symbols the docs/examples/_sdksurface example exercises carry no entry: that example is their caller.

a2a/a2atest.Cancel.reason: test fixture, called only from tests
a2a/a2atest.Cancel.target: the symbol gate learning interface-dispatch reachability; the methods stay served via Loopback

a2a/a2atest.Execute.reason: test fixture, called only from tests
a2a/a2atest.Execute.target: the symbol gate learning interface-dispatch reachability; the methods stay served via Loopback

a2a/a2atest.Loopback.reason: test fixture, called only from tests
a2a/a2atest.Loopback.target: no production caller is possible under the fixture import policy; revisit only if the policy itself changes

mcp.CallToolWithProgress.reason: Needs a live initialized MCP session to reach; the only in-repo server is the self-exec fixture inside the package's test binary, which a non-test caller cannot import.
mcp.CallToolWithProgress.target: an in-repo MCP server fixture a non-test caller can run, then this example drives one call with progress

mcp.RegisterAll.reason: Needs a live initialized MCP session to list tools from; the only in-repo server is the self-exec fixture inside the package's test binary, which a non-test caller cannot import.
mcp.RegisterAll.target: an in-repo MCP server fixture a non-test caller can run, then this example registers its tools

tools.NewScopeChecked.reason: Construction-time-validating pair to NewScope (scope.go:80, added 2026-09-07). No caller yet: an external consumer's own tool-scope type is a separate, unmigrated privilege filter. Target: an external consumer wiring tools.Scope into its own dispatcher and retiring its parallel filter, a larger follow-up, not attempted here.
tools.NewScopeChecked.target: an external consumer's dispatcher, once it adopts tools.Scope over its own privilege filter
